newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica business seeks top level talks with labour.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica business seeks top level talks with labour.

text.p: South African business on Wednesday called for key players to meet at the highest level to resolve the current impasse on new labour legislation which triggered a one-day nationwide strike on June 2.

"Negotiations cannot be held hostage by abritrary deadlines," said Business South African deputy president Leslie Boyd said, referring labour's 14-day ultimatum to business to present revised proposals on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill or face further action.
"We have to find balances between the competing demands on the labour market policies," Boyd said.
Business South Africa negotiator Adrian du Plessis said it was vital that the various partners found consensus on outstanding issues.
"Around this specific law we need consensus, otherwise it won't work."

He said that the differences between unions, government and business were deep but at the highest level it seemed there were common objectives in areas such as job creation, economic growth and labour market fairness.
"The parties are united by a broad set of common objectives and we need to find a way to translate this into legislative reality," he said.
Du Plessis said that contrary to press reports, business supported some of the core issues in the bill such as the increase in maternity leave from three to four months.
Business also agreed with an increase in annual leave and the reduction of working hours to 45 hours from 46 hours except in mining and agriculture where there were particular problems.
